teaching_point: Junctional naevus: flat, evenly pigmented brown macule (nests at the dermo-epidermal junction). Reticular pattern on dermoscopy.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Junctional naevus (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Compound naevus: slightly raised centre with a flat pigmented rim (junctional plus dermal components).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mole: compound naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Intradermal (dermal) naevus: soft, pale-pink papule. Pigment fades as the naevus matures, so a skin-coloured dome is usually benign.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mole: dermal naevus (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Miescher-type dome-shaped intradermal naevus (usually face/trunk). Long-standing, slowly enlarging, uniform.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — miescher (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Unna-type papillomatous dermal naevus (trunk/neck): soft, warty, 'bunch of grapes'. It may catch and become inflamed but is benign.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Unna naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Common acquired mole: small, symmetrical, one colour, regular edge. This is the 'normal' against which you judge an ugly duckling.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — common mole (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: regular reticular network fading at the periphery, typical of a junctional or compound naevus.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy: reticular naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: globular pattern (brown globules).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Globular naevus dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: starburst pattern (Spitz/Reed naevus). Symmetrical starbursts are often benign in children, but in adults excision is usually advised, so refer.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy: starburst naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of an atypical naevus with peripheral dots/globules. Could be an actively growing naevus or an early melanoma: needs specialist dermoscopy and monitoring or excision.
dermnet_caption: Dermoscopy of an atypical naevus with peripheral dots
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy of an atypical naevus with peripheral dots (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atypical-naevus-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of a dysplastic naevus: irregular network and multiple tones. It overlaps with melanoma.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy of a dysplastic naevus (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atypical-naevus-images

teaching_point: Giant congenital melanocytic naevus over a child's trunk and buttocks. Projected adult size over 20 cm carries the highest melanoma risk ( 5–10%). Lifelong specialist follow-up; new nodules or rapid change mean urgent review.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Congenital naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/congenital-melanocytic-naevi

teaching_point: Medium CMN (1.5–20 cm projected adult size): textured, darker, with some hair. Melanoma risk is low (around 1% or less), so monitor and photograph.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Congenital naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Hairy congenital naevus. Darkening, coarse hair and a rougher texture with age are expected benign changes; a new lump is not.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hairy congenital naevi (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: CMN with a slightly irregular outline on a limb. Congenital naevi often break ABCDE 'rules', which is why the 7-point checklist and specialist review matter more than ABCDE alone.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Congenital naevus (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/congenital-melanocytic-naevi

teaching_point: Back with numerous naevi of varying size, shape and colour. With melanoma in a first-degree relative and childhood burns this is high risk, so refer for baseline dermoscopy/photography (mole mapping).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Atypical naevi (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atypical-naevus-images

teaching_point: Many atypical naevi on the back and flank. Total naevus count over 100, or several atypical naevi, independently raises melanoma risk.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Atypical naevi (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atypical-naevus-images

teaching_point: Variably pigmented, irregular naevus marked for excision; histology showed a dysplastic naevus. Excise whole (2 mm margin) when it is clinically suspicious.
dermnet_caption: A variably-pigmented, irregularly-marginated naevus - histology showed a dysplastic naevus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A variably-pigmented, irregularly-marginated naevus - histology showed a dysplastic naevus (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atypical-naevus-images

teaching_point: Asymmetric, variably pigmented, irregular atypical naevus. Weighted 7-point: irregular shape (2) + irregular colour (2) = 4, so this meets NG12 for a suspected cancer pathway referral.
dermnet_caption: Asymmetric, variably-pigmented, and irregularly-marginated atypical naevus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Asymmetric, variably-pigmented, and irregularly-marginated atypical naevus (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atypical-naevus-images

teaching_point: Dysplastic naevus with a darker eccentric component next to a smaller dark naevus. The 'ugly duckling' sign is what patients and partners should look for.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — dysplastic (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus

teaching_point: Halo naevus: a central naevus with a symmetrical depigmented ring, common in teenagers. It is benign, but an adult with an irregular halo, or with an irregular naevus in the centre, should be referred.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Halo naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/halo-naevus

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of a halo naevus: a regular globular centre with a white halo.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Halo naevus dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/halo-naevus

teaching_point: Blue naevus: uniform slate- or steel-blue papule (deep dermal melanocytes). Stable for years is reassuring; a new or changing blue-black nodule means nodular melanoma until proven otherwise.
dermnet_caption: A blue naevus - the monochrome slate blue colour is typical
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A blue naevus - the monochrome slate blue colour is typical (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/blue-naevus

teaching_point: Classic Spitz naevus: rapidly growing pink dome in a child. Rapid growth worries parents. Refer: specialists usually excise or follow closely.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Classic Spitz naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/spitz-naevus

teaching_point: Pigmented Spitz (Reed) naevus: a dark, symmetrical papule with a starburst pattern. It looks like melanoma clinically, so refer.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pigmented Spitz naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/spitz-naevus

teaching_point: Recurrent naevus in a scar after a shave or incomplete removal ('pseudomelanoma'). Send previous histology with any referral.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Recurrent naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melanocytic-naevus
